full_judgment: 3. The plaintiffs', case, in short, is that one Abdul Gafur was the original owner of the suit plot and he sold the same to defendant Nos. 1 to 4 who were brothers on 31-10-32. Defendants No.4 Kalimuddin while in joint possession of the same property transferred his 4 annas share to his wife Safatunnessa by registered Heba bil Ewaz deed dated 22-7-42. Thereafter Safatunnessa possessed the land till 22-1-53 and then sold it to plaintiff by registered sale deed and delivered possession to him. The defendant No.1 filed a pre-emption case against the aforesaid transfer being miscellaneous case No.62 of 1956 under section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act against the plaintiff but the said Miscellaneous case was dismissed. In the meantime plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit land and then he was compelled to file the suit. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement staung that the defendant is the real owner of the entire plot of land and has purchased the same in his name and also in benami of his 3 minor brothers and that Heba bill Ewaz deed of defendant No. 4 in favour of his wife Safatunnessa was a forged document and the plaintiff has acquired no title to the land by purchase. His further case is that, he is entitled to purchase the undivided share of the suit plot which is the homestead and filed the petition suit to buy the suit land under section 4 of the Partition Act. The trial Court decreed the suit. Defendant No.1 preferred appeal and the appellate Court by its judgment and decree dated 16-7-92 upheld the trial Court's judgment. Being aggrieved at the aforesaid judgment of the appellate Court the petitioners preferred this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.
